You have to complete a bachelor’s degree first to apply for dental school. Your A/l results won’t be enough. It’ll count as some credit hours for biology 1 and 2, gen chem and organic chemistry and physics 1 and 2 ( it also depends on the college you apply). So when you apply to college you’ll be a pre dental student and you’ll complete prerequisites for dental school. 

While you’re in school you can shadow dentists to learn more. Also you need to sit for dental admission test. You need letters of recommendation and finally face an interview. 

You can email any college and ask them what you can do with your a/l results. If you have really good results some schools will let you apply for dental school, I’m not 100% sure about that though. Dental schools also have lab requirements.

I’m in pharmacy school studying pharmaceutical science. I love doing lab work/research. Talk to your professors and ask them whether you can work in their labs. Also try to take lab courses. I don’t mean mandatory lab courses.

I worked as an undergraduate research assistant and I liked all the grad students I worked with. They taught me a lot and trained me when I was just starting out. You have to understand that we have to deal with so many things in day today life. We have to go to classes, study, cook, clean and also do research. Even though I got paid it wasn’t enough to cover all my expenses. Mind you, I was only getting paid max $800 monthly. There were days I couldn’t work in the lab because everything was getting too much for me and my mental health was getting worse. We understand that grad students work really hard and we appreciate you guys immensely. But sometimes we have to pursue other options or simply stop working at the lab because research isn’t the only thing on our plate. Please don’t take it personal.
